doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Closing remarks
summary: Mead calls it a remarkable time and hopes to play to 95; Rowe praises the band and thanks him.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well we have a lot in common, we have the music, we have children who went to Hamilton and I’m really pleased to have been able to gather your thoughts about this whole thing. Is there anything that you’d like to add to what we’ve talked about?

No, I think we’ve covered it. It was a remarkable time in my life. I think back to those days with just the greatest happiness. And I’m loving playing with the Alumni All-Stars now, so music is just a happy thread and I just hope I can keep playing ‘till I’m 95 like my dad did.

Oh that’s a great thought. And as a sort of outside observer but someone who’s had the pleasure of sitting in a few times I can say that in the last number of years I’ve noticed a real jump in the band’s, the whole sound you’re putting out. It’s been great to hear.
Well come and hear us tonight — tomorrow night.
I will. All right. Well thanks for your time. It’s been a real pleasure.
